title: Comparative analysis of functional network dynamics in high and low alcohol preference mice.
authors: Wang, Zilin; Zhao, Yingying; Wang, Ze; Sun, Nongyuan; Yu, Wen; Feng, Quying; Kim, Hee Young; Ge, Feifei; Yang, Xin; Guan, Xiaowei
one_liner_zh: 该文通过c-Fos图谱和功能网络分析比较高低酒精偏好小鼠的脑区活动差异，属于神经科学行为研究，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Individual variability preference is a typical characteristic of alcohol drinking behaviors, with a higher risk for the development of alcohol use disorders (AUDs) in high alcohol preference (HP) populations. Here, we created a map of alcohol-related brain regions through c-Fos profiling, and comparatively investigated the differences of functional neural networks between the HP mice and low alcohol preference (LP) mice. We found that neuronal activity in some brain regions, such as ventral tegmental area (VTA), was altered in both HP and LP mice, indicating that these neurons were universally sensitive to alcohol. Most importantly, several brain regions, such as the prefrontal cortex and insular cortex, exhibited significantly higher c-Fos expression in HP mice than that in LP mice and displayed broader and stronger neural connections across brain networks, suggesting that these brain regions are the potential targets for individual alcohol preference. Graph theory-based analysis unraveled a decrease in brain modularity in HP networks, yet with more centralized connection patterns, and maintained higher communication efficiency and redundancy. Furthermore, LP mice switched the central network hubs, with the key differential network centered on nucleus accumbens shell (NAc Sh), nucleus accumbens core (NAc C), VTA, and anterior insular cortex (AIC), indicating that these brain regions and related neural circuits, such as NAc Sh-AIC may be involved in regulating individual alcohol preference. These results provide novel insights into the neural connections governing individual preferences to alcohol consumption, which may contribute to AUDs prediction and pharmacotherapy.
abstract_zh: 个体变异性偏好是饮酒行为的典型特征，高酒精偏好（HP）人群发展为酒精使用障碍（AUDs）的风险更高。在此，我们通过c-Fos图谱绘制了酒精相关脑区图谱，并比较研究了HP小鼠与低酒精偏好（LP）小鼠之间功能神经网络的差异。我们发现，某些脑区（如腹侧被盖区（VTA））的神经元活动在HP和LP小鼠中均发生改变，表明这些神经元对酒精普遍敏感。最重要的是，前额叶皮层和岛叶皮层等几个脑区在HP小鼠中的c-Fos表达显著高于LP小鼠，并在脑网络中展现出更广泛和更强的神经连接，提示这些脑区是个体酒精偏好的潜在靶点。基于图论的分析揭示，HP网络中的脑模块性降低，但连接模式更为集中，并保持了更高的通信效率和冗余性。此外，LP小鼠切换了中枢网络枢纽，关键差异网络以伏隔核壳部（NAc Sh）、伏隔核核心部（NAc C）、VTA和前岛叶皮层（AIC）为中心，表明这些脑区及相关神经回路（如NAc Sh-AIC）可能参与调节个体酒精偏好。这些结果为调控个体饮酒偏好的神经连接提供了新见解，可能有助于AUDs的预测和药物治疗。
